## Context / Problem

Making OperationSnapshot authoritative for LLM operations (gaudy-working-mantaray) migrates `LLMConfig.from_env` call sites and threads a snapshot-derived projection through the gate/workflow entry points. The two llm modules carrying the densest from_env/composition logic are within a few lines of the hard 800-LOC module-size cap (`.github/module-size-limit.txt` = 800), so that threading would breach the CI module-size gate on first edit:

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` = 799 (`LLMConfig.from_env` plus 14 from_env/gate references)
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` = 796

Create headroom FIRST via behavior-preserving extraction along existing call-graph seams so the config-threading cutover lands without breaching the module-size gate. This story adds no snapshot-threading logic; it only relocates existing clusters.

## Approach

Extract cohesive existing clusters into sibling modules per the AGENTS.md module-size policy (existing seams only; target 200-500 LOC; never create a module < 100 LOC; never split mechanically):

- `llm/config.py`: move the primitive env/file reader helpers (`_env_truthy`, `_read_llm_file_table`, `_llm_str_source`, `_llm_str`, `_llm_int`, `_llm_float`, `_llm_drain_mode`) into a new sibling module `llm/config_readers.py`. `config.py` re-imports every one of them (`from .config_readers import (...)  # noqa: F401`) at module top level, mirroring the EXISTING `gate_context` re-export pattern documented in `config.py`'s own L41-47 docstring. `LLMConfig.from_env` (the sole in-repo caller of this cluster) is NOT moved and keeps calling these names as bare references — so its lookup resolves through `config.py`'s own namespace (its `__globals__`), exactly as `from_env` already does for the re-exported `gate_context` names. This is what keeps the ~15 existing `monkeypatch.setattr(rebar.llm.config, "_read_llm_file_table", ...)` (and sibling helper) test seams live. `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` also imports `_read_llm_file_table` directly from `rebar.llm.config` — it keeps working unchanged because the re-export preserves that import path.
- `llm/plan_review/__init__.py`: move ONLY the five pure/leaf functions of the score-floor / completion-floor cluster — `_apply_floor_to_verdict`, `_score_floor_novelty`, `_apply_completion_floor_to_verdict`, `_classify_completion`, `_group_blocking_fix_units` — into a new sibling module `llm/plan_review/floors.py`, re-imported into `__init__.py` (`from .floors import (...)  # noqa: F401`). The two orchestrator wrappers, `_maybe_apply_rising_floor` and `_maybe_apply_completion_floor`, STAY in `__init__.py` (not moved) because they are both (a) the entry points `_run_plan_review` calls directly, and (b) the functions whose internal calls to the five moved leaves must keep resolving through `__init__.py`'s own namespace so that `monkeypatch.setattr(plan_review, "_score_floor_novelty", ...)` (test_plan_review_rising_floor.py) and `monkeypatch.setattr(plan_review, "_classify_completion", ...)` (test_completion_floor.py) continue to intercept the call as today. `monkeypatch.setattr(plan_review, "_maybe_apply_rising_floor"/"_maybe_apply_completion_floor"/"_group_blocking_fix_units", ...)` (test_plan_review_sidecar_heldout.py) keeps working regardless, because its caller `_run_plan_review` also stays in `__init__.py`.
- **`_verifier_cfg` stays in `__init__.py`** (it is used by other code that stays there too, e.g. `review_plan`/`_run_plan_review`). The two moved leaves that call it (`_score_floor_novelty`, `_classify_completion`) reach it via a **lazy import inside the function body** — `from rebar.llm.plan_review import _verifier_cfg` at the top of each function, not a module-top-level `from . import _verifier_cfg` in `floors.py`. This avoids the circular-import/load-order hazard that a top-level cross-import would create (`__init__.py` does `from .floors import (...)` at its own module top, so `floors.py` cannot also top-level-import back from `__init__` without a cycle); by the time either function actually runs, `rebar.llm.plan_review` is fully initialized, so the lazy import resolves cleanly. This mirrors the lazy-import style `_score_floor_novelty` and `_classify_completion` already use for `rebar.llm.runner`, `rebar.llm.review_kernel.verify`, and `from . import passes`.

`LLMConfig`, `review_plan`, and the public plan_review imports keep working; only internal call sites for the five moved plan_review leaves change module (moving with them), while `from_env`'s and the two floor-wrapper's own call sites are untouched.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/` — extract the named clusters into new sibling modules (`config_readers.py`, `plan_review/floors.py`) and update imports only. Does NOT modify `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`, which is owned by the runner refactor (hurt-antigorite-genet), to avoid a collision.
- `tests/unit/`, `tests/unit/workflow/`, and `tests/external/` — import-path updates only for ordinary consumers, PLUS two named consumers that pin a physical module path/text and must be repointed (not merely re-imported):
  - `tests/unit/test_env_registry_helper_coverage.py` AST-parses `config.py`'s source TEXT by path (`_CONFIG_PY = src/rebar/llm/config.py`) to enumerate `_llm_*`/`_llm_drain_mode` helpers. Its `_CONFIG_PY` control must be re-pointed to `src/rebar/llm/config_readers.py` (the file that now contains those helpers), or extended to also parse `config_readers.py`, so `_llm_helpers_with_env_arg()` / the drain-mode probe keep finding the moved names.
  - `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py` hard-codes `_score_floor_novelty`'s RunRequest construction site in `_EXPECTED_RUN_REQUEST_SITES` as `'llm/plan_review/__init__.py::_score_floor_novelty'`; update that entry to `'llm/plan_review/floors.py::_score_floor_novelty'` to match the moved leaf's new AST-derived site key.

## Testing

Existing llm and plan-review suites (including `tests/unit/workflow/` and `tests/external/`) pass unchanged (behavior-preserving) — in particular every existing `monkeypatch.setattr(rebar.llm.config, "_read_llm_file_table", ...)` site and every `monkeypatch.setattr(plan_review, "<floor-helper>", ...)` site in `test_plan_review_rising_floor.py`, `test_completion_floor.py`, `test_completion_floor_e2e.py`, `test_blocking_fix_unit_grouping.py`, and `test_plan_review_sidecar_heldout.py` keeps intercepting the same call it does today. `test_env_registry_helper_coverage.py` and `test_subcall_class_selection.py` are updated per Scope above and continue to pass. Module-size gate, per-function complexity ratchet, lint, and typecheck pass. No new CI-provider, network, or Docker dependency is introduced (portable default suite).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `llm/config.py` and `llm/plan_review/__init__.py` are each comfortably below 800 LOC (target <= 700), achieved only by extracting existing call-graph clusters into sibling modules (`config_readers.py`, `plan_review/floors.py`).
- [ ] No newly created module is below 100 LOC, and no extraction is mechanical.
- [ ] Every existing monkeypatch seam targeting a moved helper via its ORIGINAL module (`rebar.llm.config.<helper>` / `rebar.llm.plan_review.<helper>`) keeps intercepting the same call site it does today.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_env_registry_helper_coverage.py`'s `_CONFIG_PY` path control and `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py`'s `_EXPECTED_RUN_REQUEST_SITES` entry are updated to the new module locations and continue to pass.
- [ ] `floors.py`'s use of `_verifier_cfg` (which stays in `__init__.py`) is via a lazy in-function import — no top-level circular import between `plan_review/__init__.py` and `plan_review/floors.py`.
- [ ] Behavior is unchanged: existing llm/provider/plan-review suites (`tests/unit/`, `tests/unit/workflow/`, `tests/external/`) pass.
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py`'s direct `from rebar.llm.config import _read_llm_file_table` (or equivalent) keeps working unchanged.
- [ ] `llm/runner.py` is not modified here, avoiding collision with hurt-antigorite-genet.
- [ ] Module-size gate, per-function complexity ratchet, lint, and typecheck all pass.
